The Inferno is a seventy-five-ton Inner Sphere OmniMech rushed into production by StarCorps Industries on Crofton following the fall of New Avalon to the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery during the Dark Age. Introduced in 3146, the design grew out of several improved survivability projects that StarCorps had been developing as testbed concepts, though only one of those made it into the final production model. With generous pod space and heavy armor protection, the Inferno was designed as a flexible heavy platform for the depleted Armed Forces of the Federated Suns.

StarCorps marketed the design with characteristic boldness, promising that the Draconis Combine would not take another inch of Davion soil as long as the Inferno still raged. The chassis quickly became popular within the AFFS, valued both for its combat flexibility and its forgiving handling characteristics that made it accessible to inexperienced MechWarriors.

The Inferno is built around a standard GM 300 fusion engine and a compact gyro, a combination that frees considerable space in the center torso for heavy weapons. StarCorps engineers took advantage of the StarFrame Heavy Endo Steel chassis to maximize pod capacity while maintaining robust armor protection. In every configuration, the primary weapons are mounted in the center torso (the most heavily armored section of the ’Mech) with additional firepower carried in the side torsos, often in over-the-shoulder mounts. The arms are deliberately left free of weapons, instead equipped with armored gauntlets that allow the Inferno to engage effectively in close combat.

The Prime configuration exemplifies this philosophy, mounting a Heavy PPC as its primary weapon alongside two Medium Re-Engineered Lasers and a pair of MML-5 launchers that provide tactical flexibility between direct and indirect fire support. The design is not particularly fast nor does it carry overwhelming firepower, but its combination of generous pod space, solid protection, and easy handling make it effective for both veteran and inexperienced MechWarriors.

The center torso pod space does suffer from an innovative but insufficiently shielded power link to the fusion engine, producing brief electromagnetic interference that can impair some electronic systems. This was deemed an acceptable trade-off given the urgent need to rebuild AFFS regiments.

The Inferno’s development was driven by desperation. When New Avalon fell to the Draconis Combine, the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns lost not only their capital but significant manufacturing capacity and strategic depth. StarCorps Industries on Crofton, already engaged in survivability research and testbed projects, was pressed to accelerate development into full production. The result was a design that prioritized practical combat effectiveness over technical perfection.

The AFFS prioritized Inferno shipments to front-line garrisons defending against further Combine incursions, particularly newly formed or rebuilt regiments that needed reliable heavy ’Mechs quickly. The design proved particularly effective as a platform for integrating new MechWarriors, with its easy handling characteristics and forgiving piloting requirements. StarCorps addressed concerns that the Inferno was merely a training platform by providing a shipment of ClanTech-configured Infernos to the Davion Guards, demonstrating the chassis’s ability to carry advanced weapons effectively.

The Kestrel Grenadiers received a lance of Infernos for Operation Perceval. Though not ideally suited to the raiding operations that defined that campaign, the ’Mechs were assigned to base security on Remagen, where they proved effective at harassing enemy landing zones and forcing attackers to disperse their efforts. When Task Force Tsujigiri arrived to end the Federated Suns’ raids, the Infernos engaged each landing in succession, disrupting coordination and keeping the enemy guessing. The Combine pursuit eventually overwhelmed the Grenadiers, trapping them between pursuers and an offloading company.

Infernos have also seen service with the Capellan March Militia, deployed alongside fire support vehicles and battle armor in combined-arms formations. During operations on Taygeta in 3146, Inferno-equipped command lances demonstrated the design’s effectiveness in defensive operations, holding fortified positions against Capellan assaults while protecting attached artillery batteries.

The Jenner is a relatively modern design, first constructed in 2784 by Diplan Mechyards of Ozawa under contract to House Kurita. Originally developed for the Star League Defense Force, the design was secretly acquired by the Draconis Combine after Kerensky's Exodus. Designed as a fast, hit-and-run guerrilla fighter, the Jenner would form the foundation for highly mobile lances that became a hallmark of DCMS doctrine.

Faster than most opponents while carrying respectable firepower for its weight class, the Jenner became synonymous with Combine military power, remaining the exclusive property of House Kurita for over fifty years. However, the Jenner's reputation was forever tarnished by its prominent role in the Kentares Massacre of 2796, when waves of Jenners carried out Coordinator Jinjiro Kurita's infamous directive.

Among the fastest 'Mechs of its era, the Jenner packs impressive firepower at close range. Its optimum engagement range is 30 to 90 meters, and its speed and jump capability make it exceptionally hard to hit. The Jenner can move in quickly, deliver its attack, and retreat before sustaining serious damage. Because the Argra 3L medium lasers are the primary armament, the 'Mech can operate for extended periods without ammunition concerns during deep raids.

The Thunderstroke SRM-4 provides additional hitting power for decisive moments, though the limited ammunition supply requires careful management during prolonged operations. Combined, these weapons give the Jenner more firepower than most light BattleMechs and several medium designs as well. Though an alpha strike generates significant heat, pilots use their impressive jump capability to buy cooling time between engagements.

The Jenner lacks arms for physical attacks, a deliberate design choice given its low tonnage. The four tons of armor provide only light protection compared to similar weight classes, making pilot skill and mobility essential to survival in sustained combat.

Diplan was originally contracted by the SLDF to produce Jenners, with the first models joining the Exodus fleet in 2784. Once Kerensky disappeared, Kurita agents secretly negotiated with Diplan to continue the contract under the noses of FedSuns peacekeepers on Ozawa. When the DCMS began its offensive in 2786, Kurita MechWarriors infiltrated under civilian cover launched the first wave directly from Diplan's warehouses.

Despite the outbreak of the First Succession War, construction continued at Diplan Mechyard's factory on Ozawa until a raw materials shortage halted assembly in 2815, though chassis production continued. In 2823, production resumed on Ozawa, with some 3,000 chassis shipped to a Diplan subsidiary on Luthien for final fittings and assembly. By 2830, both production lines were producing 1,350 Jenners a year. The sheer destruction of the Succession Wars took their toll when the Ozawa facilities were destroyed in 2837, and unexplained explosion destroyed the remaining assembly plant on Luthien in 2848, ending Jenner production.

By 2840, the Federated Suns and Lyran Commonwealth had obtained operational Jenners through battlefield salvage. By 2845, all Successor States had access to the design, although it continued to be primarily a Kurita 'Mech. Despite the huge production volumes of the era, the Jenner never became very prevalent beyond the Draconis Combine. A favorite tactic of Jenner lances was to gang up on larger 'Mechs and unleash a devastating alpha strike, often with one or two 'Mechs equipped with inferno rounds.

Rebuilding a Jenner production line on Luthien became a top priority under Gunji-no-Kanrei Theodore Kurita. With ComStar aid, Luthien Armor Works finally reopened the line in 3046. The recovery of lost technology made the Jenner a prime candidate for upgrades, though LAW deliberately avoided radical changes to preserve the original's core advantages. The spectacularly brutal start to the Jihad led many units to return to stockpiles of once-shunned Jenners for replacement machines, proving their value once again.

The Juliano was the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth's signature assault BattleMech, introduced in 3116 as the culmination of that realm's longstanding ambition to develop a native assault-weight design. Named after Juliano Marik, the first Captain-General of the Free Worlds League, the ninety-ton 'Mech was produced by Irian BattleMechs Unlimited at their Angell II facility. Designed as an all-purpose combatant capable of filling virtually any tactical role demanded of an assault 'Mech, the Juliano employs a distinctive mix of Inner Sphere and Clan technologies to achieve an excellent balance of firepower, protection, and mobility. Following twenty years of distinguished service as the signature unit of the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth, the Juliano was inherited by the reformed Free Worlds League Military, where it has become a mainstay of assault lances across the League's front-line formations.

The Juliano achieves its versatility through an Irian Tonans Endo-Composite chassis powered by a Hermes 360 XL engine, giving the ninety-ton machine a respectable top speed of 64 kph for its weight class. Protection comes from over sixteen tons of Durallex Guardian II Light Ferro-Fibrous armor supplemented by CASE II equipment in both arms, ensuring ammunition detonations do not prove fatal. Engineers further reinforced the cockpit armor to improve pilot survivability in prolonged engagements.

The 'Mech's primary firepower centers on three Diverse Optics Sunbeam Extended-Range Large Lasers distributed across the torso sections, providing devastating long-range striking power. These are complemented by three Diverse Optics Sunfire Extended-Range Medium Lasers for intermediate engagements and four arm-mounted Clan-specification Pattern J6 Streak SRM-6 launchers that deliver punishing close-range salvos with exceptional ammunition efficiency. A specialized combat computer was installed on the advice of prototype test pilots to manage the significant heat generated by the laser battery, though inexperienced MechWarriors can still push the design to critical overheat by firing too aggressively. This combination of weapons allows the Juliano to remain effective across all engagement ranges and continue fighting long after ammunition-dependent opponents have exhausted their stores.

The Karhu was introduced in 3079 as the first Clan-technology OmniMech produced by Odin Manufacturing for the Ghost Bear Dominion. Named after the Finnish word for "bear," the sixty-five-ton heavy OmniMech was designed to fill the Dominion's need for a fast cavalry platform built with the latest Clan technology. Odin Manufacturing, based on the former Free Rasalhague Republic world of Orestes, won a competitive contract against their chief rival Bergan Industries in 3077, delivering a design that earned a fierce reputation as a frontline cavalry 'Mech despite lingering questions about its electronics reliability. The Karhu remains a symbol of the Dominion's industrial ambitions and a mainstay of its frontline clusters.

The Karhu is built around a Beowulf 4 Enhanced endo steel chassis powered by a Pitban 325-rated extra-light engine, giving the sixty-five-ton OmniMech a respectable top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour. Ten and a half tons of Compound A2F ferro-fibrous armor provide solid protection for its weight class, while twelve fixed double heat sinks manage baseline waste heat across its varied configurations. This combination of speed, protection, and Clan-grade construction leaves an impressive thirty tons of available pod space for mission-specific equipment.

The Prime configuration reflects the design's appeal to the KungsArmé tradition of physical combat, mounting a retractable blade sculpted into a fearsome three-pronged claw alongside a plasma cannon in the right arm. An ER PPC and ER medium laser in the left arm provide ranged firepower, while improved jump jets grant exceptional battlefield mobility. However, Odin's relative inexperience with Clan technology has manifested in documented electronics reliability issues. The firm reused the Beowulf's proven Dash-2 Standard communications system and Blade 12 targeting computer to save development time, but intermittent compatibility glitches with Clan-manufactured components have plagued the design in the field, a problem technicians attribute to fundamental incompatibilities between Inner Sphere electronics architectures and Clan equipment.

The Karhu's development was born from the merger of the Free Rasalhague Republic and the Ghost Bear Dominion, which opened Clan technology to Inner Sphere manufacturers for the first time. For Odin Manufacturing, the merger represented both opportunity and challenge. Their Orestes production facility had been damaged by Word of Blake raids in the late 3060s, and the demands of the Jihad forced them to continue producing existing Inner Sphere designs while simultaneously planning their transition to Clan-technology manufacturing. By 3077, when the Dominion announced a competition for a new heavy OmniMech, Odin was finally ready to make the leap.

The competition between Odin and their rival Bergan Industries proved fierce. Odin identified Bergan as their primary competitor and designed the Karhu specifically to outperform whatever Bergan produced, while simultaneously launching a marketing campaign rooted in Rasalhagian nationalism aimed at former KungsArme officers within the Dominion touman. This strategy proved effective, and Odin won the contract in 3079 with a design that was widely acknowledged as technologically superior to Bergan's competing entry, the Arcas.

First deployed in 3079, the Karhu arrived too late to participate in Operation SCOUR but rapidly became a fixture in the Dominion's frontline clusters. Paired frequently with the Ursus II, the Karhu earned a reputation as a cavalry 'Mech, flanking opponents while heavier designs drew fire at close range. During the Jihad's final stages and the early Republic era, Karhus were concentrated in frontline formations alongside Vultures and other OmniMechs, forming the mobile striking arm of Dominion combined-arms doctrine.

The design's success has not been without controversy. Competition between Odin and Bergan Industries has grown increasingly bitter, with Odin officials publicly disparaging Bergan as "that Capellan company with their Combine workers." Requests for Orestes-built 'Mechs are noticeably higher among Rasalhagian warriors as a result of this rivalry. The Ghost Bear Council has expressed concern over this infighting and has requested that representatives of both companies exercise restraint, though reports suggest the merchants are too deeply engaged in their competition to easily comply.

The Karhu's documented electronics reliability issues have been a persistent concern throughout its service history. Technicians have traced the intermittent glitches to fundamental incompatibilities between the Inner Sphere-designed communications and targeting systems and the Clan-manufactured components they interface with, citing similar problems on Beowulfs retrofitted with Clan equipment. Odin has denied culpability, but the issue remains unresolved and represents an ongoing maintenance burden for Dominion technicians. Despite this flaw, the Karhu's combination of speed, firepower, and pod flexibility has ensured its continued prominence in the Dominion's order of battle, with the 2nd Legion of Vega's attack on the Orestes production line in 3099 emphasizing both the design's strategic importance and its vulnerability to disruption.

text.overview:
The Incubus, designated the Vixen by Inner Sphere intelligence analysts, is a thirty-ton Clan light BattleMech first produced in 2954 during the Golden Century. Originally a Clan Jade Falcon garrison design, the Incubus was purpose-built for the ritualized single combat Trials that are a cornerstone of Clan warrior culture. Its combination of speed, firepower, and easily adjustable weapon systems made it ideal for duels between MechWarriors and augmented Elementals, where individual weapons could be powered down to balance the engagement.

Despite its origins as a dueling platform, the Incubus proved capable enough to earn a place in second-line combat formations across multiple Clans. Its relatively high cost for a garrison 'Mech initially puzzled Spheroid observers, who did not yet understand the central role of Trials in Clan society. Production spread to numerous Clan holdings over the centuries, making the Incubus one of the most widely distributed second-line light 'Mechs in Clan space.
text.capabilities:
The Incubus achieves remarkable performance for its weight class through its use of a 270-rated XL engine, endo steel frame, and five and a half tons of ferro-fibrous armor. This combination gives the thirty-ton design a top speed of 151 kilometers per hour, making it one of the fastest light 'Mechs in any Clan touman. The generous armor protection provides surprising survivability for a design of this tonnage, giving pilots confidence in both Trials and garrison engagements.

The standard armament centers on a large pulse laser mounted in a semi-modular "rifle" configuration in the right arm, a design feature reminiscent of classic Inner Sphere designs like the Wolverine and BattleMaster. This placement allows rapid field replacement of the primary weapon, and several variants exploit this modularity to mount different armament packages. Supporting fire comes from a pair of ER medium lasers and four machine guns distributed across the side torsos, providing effective anti-infantry capability alongside solid medium-range firepower.

The extensive all-energy secondary armament and ten double heat sinks are well suited to the controlled environment of Clan Trials, where pilots routinely fight with reduced weapon loads. In sustained battlefield engagements, however, the design can generate problematic heat levels if all weapons are fired continuously, a trade-off most pilots accept given the 'Mech's intended role.
text.deployment: A radical departure from earlier configurations, this variant employs an XXL engine to free tonnage for an ER PPC and SRM-6 in the arms, complemented by six ER micro lasers split between the side torsos. The addition of talons makes the design a capable physical combatant. Initially associated with Clan Hell's Horses Mongol warriors, the design is attributed to Clan Sea Fox production and has seen wide distribution in the Dark Age era.
text.battleHistory:
The Incubus emerged during the Golden Century as a Clan Jade Falcon design intended specifically for the ritualized Trials that permeate Clan society. First produced in 2954, the design quickly spread beyond its originators as other Clans recognized its value as both a dueling platform and a capable garrison 'Mech. Clan Steel Viper established production at New Kent Armorworks on New Kent, while Clan Ice Hellion began manufacturing at the Hector MechWorks Facility Beta. Clan Coyote operated a line at Complex H-4 on Homer, and Clan Burrock produced the design at the Albion MMA Complex on Albion before their Absorption by Clan Star Adder.

The Incubus first came to Inner Sphere attention during the Clan Invasion of 3049, when intelligence analysts sighted it among Jade Falcon garrison forces and assigned the reporting name "Vixen." Its purpose baffled Spheroid observers until the importance of Trials in Clan culture became better understood. The design served throughout the Invasion era in garrison and second-line roles across multiple Clans, its widespread availability making it a common sight in rear-area formations.

The Wars of Reaving dramatically reshaped the Incubus's production theater. Clan Steel Viper's Annihilation ended production at New Kent. The Burrock Absorption had earlier transferred the Albion facility to Clan Star Adder, though production there also eventually ceased. Clan Ice Hellion's destruction saw their Hector facility pass through Clan Goliath Scorpion and eventually to Clan Coyote control. Tokasha MechWorks Alpha, which had produced the design under Clan Ghost Bear ownership, passed to Clan Hell's Horses and then to Clan Sea Fox successor interests.

Clan Hell's Horses played a crucial role in the Incubus's evolution. Inspired by Clan Diamond Shark's "Phoenix" renovation program, the Horses developed a thoroughly updated version following their recapture of Tokasha MechWorks Alpha, incorporating newer weapons technology while maintaining the design's core dueling purpose. Clan Ice Hellion copied this redesign to create their own variant, examples of which fell into Cloud Cobra and Star Adder hands following the Hellions' ill-fated trade mission to the Tanis system.

In the post-Jihad and Dark Age eras, Clan Sea Fox emerged as a major producer through their CSF Titanic Mobile Production Facility, introducing several new variants and selling the design widely. Clan Coyote continued production on Homer into the early Republic era, though the facility's long-term status remains uncertain. The Incubus remains a valued second-line design well into the ilClan era, its enduring popularity a sign of the soundness of its original design philosophy.

text.deployment: Alternate Configuration A trades the Prime’s versatility for raw stopping power, mounting an ER PPC in the center torso paired with a Gauss rifle in the left torso. Two Medium X-Pulse Lasers provide accurate secondary fire at shorter ranges. CASE II protection in the left torso guards against catastrophic ammunition detonation from the Gauss rifle’s two tons of stored rounds. This configuration excels as a direct-fire support platform, capable of delivering devastating strikes at extended range.

Alternate Configuration B emphasizes long-range indirect fire support. An ER PPC serves as the primary weapon, supplemented by paired LRM-15 launchers mounted in the side torsos, each with two tons of ammunition protected by CASE II. Two ER Small Lasers provide a last-resort close defense capability, while an additional double heat sink helps manage heat generated by the energy weapons. This loadout allows the Inferno to operate effectively behind front lines, delivering sustained missile barrages while keeping enemies at arm’s length.

Alternate Configuration C centers on a Thunderbolt 15 missile launcher in the center torso, providing devastating single-target punch at medium to long range. MML-5 launchers in each side torso supplement the main weapon with flexible fire support, while ER Medium Lasers in each torso round out the loadout for close-range engagements. Ample ammunition storage for both the Thunderbolt and MML systems ensures sustained combat endurance, all protected by CASE II bays in both side torsos.

Alternate Configuration R distinguishes itself through the use of Clan-specification weapons, reflecting StarCorps’ access to advanced technology during the ilClan era. The center torso mounts an ER PPC and a pair of ER Large Lasers tied into a Clan-grade targeting computer, delivering devastating accuracy at extended range. Two Clan SRM-6 launchers in the side torsos provide close-range punch, sharing a single ton of ammunition in a CASE II-protected bay. Seven additional double heat sinks are required to manage the massive heat load generated by the energy-heavy loadout, making this the most firepower-intensive configuration available.

text.overview:
The Inquisitor II is a 50-ton SecurityMech developed by Irian BattleMechs Unlimited as a heavier and more capable successor to the original 35-ton Inquisitor. Introduced during the Dark Age era, the design was created specifically to safeguard the megacorporation's production facilities against increasingly sophisticated threats that had outpaced the capabilities of the lighter Inquisitor.

Classified as an advanced IndustrialMech, the Inquisitor II blurs the line between civilian security platform and military hardware more dramatically than its predecessor. Unlike the original Inquisitor, which was widely sold on the open market, the Inquisitor II has been primarily retained as a proprietary asset, though a non-proprietary variant has been offered to interested customers.
text.capabilities:
Built around an ITW 200 fusion engine, the Inquisitor II achieves a modest top speed of 64.8 kilometers per hour, slower than its lighter predecessor, but adequate for facility defense operations. Seven tons of Irian HardCase heavy industrial armor provide protection comparable to a light BattleMech, a significant consideration for a platform that may face militarized intruders. A Beagle active probe enhances the 'Mech's surveillance capabilities, allowing it to detect hidden units and concealed personnel throughout a facility's perimeter.

The Inquisitor II's primary armament stands as a dramatic upgrade over the original design. A Wildfire TSEMP cannon allows the pilot to use the 'Mech's fusion engine to generate a tight-stream electromagnetic pulse capable of disrupting enemy electronics and potentially shutting down hostile combat units entirely. An Imperator Napoleon light autocannon mounted in the right arm provides sustained ranged firepower with the flexibility of multiple ammunition types, while an Irian Weapon Works Class 4 SRM launcher handles close-range engagements. All weapons are managed through an advanced fire control system that grants accuracy on par with military-grade BattleMechs.

Learning from the original Inquisitor's most criticized flaw, the Inquisitor II incorporates CASE II protection for its ammunition stores, significantly improving pilot survivability in the event of an ammunition detonation.
text.deployment: This variant adjusts the Inquisitor II's equipment loadout to better address specific operational requirements encountered during facility security operations in the post-Republic era. Documented in later technical bulletins, this configuration shares the same 50-ton ITW Heavy Industrial chassis and general design philosophy as the base ITW-200 while incorporating refinements based on field experience from active security deployments across Irian Technologies' network of production facilities.
text.battleHistory:
The Inquisitor II emerged from Irian BattleMechs Unlimited's assessment that evolving threats to corporate infrastructure demanded a more capable security platform than the original Inquisitor could provide. As raiding and piracy intensified during the Dark Age, particularly after the collapse of the HPG network and the subsequent breakdown of centralized authority, factory complexes became increasingly attractive targets for desperate military forces and organized banditry. The 35-ton Inquisitor, while effective against conventional criminal threats, lacked the firepower to deter or engage militarized opponents.

The introduction of the Inquisitor II during the Republic era represented a significant investment by Irian BattleMechs Unlimited in self-defense capability. The inclusion of a TSEMP cannon (technology typically reserved for military applications) signaled the megacorporation's willingness to push the boundaries of what constituted acceptable corporate security hardware. The weapon's ability to disable enemy 'Mechs without causing permanent structural damage aligned well with the corporate philosophy of neutralizing threats while minimizing collateral damage to valuable industrial infrastructure.

Production has remained centered on Irian throughout the design's operational history. The factory weathered political transitions from the Republic of the Sphere through the brief period of independence during the early Dark Age before returning to Free Worlds League control. Through each transition, the Inquisitor II has continued to serve its primary role as guardian of Irian Technologies' industrial assets, with the ITW-200 remaining a proprietary design while the Peacemaker variant has been offered to external customers seeking similar anti-'Mech security capability.

text.deployment: This custom configuration drops all jump jets in favor of two additional medium lasers mounted in the torsos and an additional half ton of armor, maximizing coverage. The result is a ground-bound but heavily armed and armored variant suited for sustained firefights rather than hit-and-run tactics. By sacrificing the Jenner's signature mobility, this configuration gains raw firepower and durability that makes it better suited to defensive operations and holding actions where speed is less critical than staying power.

Extensively modified over the years to aid its role as a spotter, this custom variant originally traded two medium lasers for extra armor. Prior to the War of 3039, it was outfitted with an experimental endo steel chassis and ferro-fibrous armor, allowing the SRM-4 launcher to be replaced with a Narc missile beacon carrying three tons of homing pods.

text.overview: The Jenner has been the stalwart of DCMS light lances for centuries. The JR7-N combines the frame of the -C4 model with more conventional weapons. Heavy ferro-fibrous armor provides nearly maximum protection, and CASE II protects the vulnerable XL engine. The JR7-N improved its scouting and raiding abilities with increased jump range and a Beagle Active Probe. Careful pilots have learned to stagger weapons fire and jumping to avoid overheating.
text.notableUnits: MechWarrior Savara Lohk: Savara Lohk is an average pilot from an average world fighting for an average unit. Individually these details suggest Lohk is unremarkable, but taken as a whole they suggest something more. We suspect she is an agent of some organization. She is most likely ISF, given that the Second Dieron Regulars were heavilyreorganized following Tai-shu Katana Tormark’s support of the Nova Cat rebellion. Those personnel are known entities though, so Lohk could be an agent from another House or Clan. This could be used to our advantage.:br::br::tab:During the conquest of Fomalhaut earlier this year, Lohk was instrumental in tracking down the commander of the Aquamarines mercenary command. Having gone to ground, the mercenaries plagued the Second for weeks, even attacking their cantonment directly. During one such attack, Lohk identified the mercenary commander, enabling the Second to capture him. Following his execution, the mercenaries disappeared into the populace, with the Second as yet failing to locate them.

text.deployment: The prototype JR7-X mounted only two medium lasers and featured a large laser in a directional mount mimicking a turret. This original configuration suffered from numerous problems, as the turret-mounted lasers proved too fragile for production and the medium lasers' targeting systems were bug-ridden. Few if any of these prototype Jenners survived into the thirty-first century.

text.overview: The Jinggau emerged from the Shengli Arms facility on Victoria in early 3059, a product of the Capellan Confederation's Xin Sheng revitalization movement and the unlikely assistance of the Word of Blake's Toyama faction. The sixty-five-ton heavy cavalry design was one of several BattleMechs developed using the old Star League-era production infrastructure on Victoria, with Blake technicians helping to refurbish the facility as repayment of a personal debt owed to Chancellor Sun-Tzu Liao. The name Jinggau, reportedly meaning "siren," proved apt, the design was built to announce its presence on the battlefield with devastating force rather than operate from the shadows. Despite early complications during development, the Jinggau would prove itself a formidable combatant and a cornerstone of the modern Capellan Confederation Armed Forces.
text.capabilities:
The Jinggau is designed to wade into the thick of combat rather than skulk at the edges of an engagement. Built on a lightweight Chariot Type II Endo Steel chassis and powered by a VOX 325 XL engine, the design achieves a top speed exceeding eighty-six kilometers per hour while five Hellespont Leaper jump jets provide one hundred and fifty meters of jump capability, allowing it to close rapidly across almost any terrain. Over eleven tons of armor give the Jinggau excellent survivability for its weight class, ensuring it can absorb punishment while pressing the attack.

The primary weapon is the formidable Zhi-tong-yao Gauss rifle, capable of striking targets at extreme range and delivering punishing kinetic impacts that can stagger even assault-class machines. Sixteen rounds of ammunition allow the Jinggau to sustain fire through several engagements before requiring resupply. As the range closes, four Diverse Optics extended-range medium lasers and a precise Raker-IV medium pulse laser provide withering close-range firepower that exploits any weakened armor the Gauss rifle has already compromised.

The reliance on an XL engine represents the design's primary vulnerability, a penetrating hit to the side torso can prove catastrophic. Additionally, the two-ton ammunition bay for the Gauss rifle presents an explosion risk if the internal structure is breached, though the weapon itself does not generate waste heat. Thirteen double heat sinks manage the thermal load effectively under normal combat conditions.
text.deployment: Debuting in 3146 following the Capellan recapture of Victoria, this variant stands as a radical modernization of the Jinggau chassis. The explosive Gauss rifle is replaced by a Clan Sea Fox-supplied Type DDS "Kingston" extended-range PPC, eliminating ammunition dependency while maintaining comparable damage output. The medium pulse laser is upgraded to a Ceres Arms Model X medium X-Pulse model, and the extended-range medium lasers transition to Diverse Optics Sunfire models. Beneath the surface, the most significant changes are Triple Strength Myomer and a supercharger that can push the design to a staggering one hundred and twenty kilometers per hour when the myomer is active. Armor protection increases to thirteen tons, and four tons of internal component armor protect the cockpit, gyro, and hip actuators. Seventeen double heat sinks manage the thermal load, with pilots able to activate the TSM with relative ease during sustained combat.
text.battleHistory:
The Jinggau's origins are inextricably linked to the Capellan Confederation's Xin Sheng movement and the restoration of the Star League-era production facility on Victoria that became Shengli Arms. Toward the end of 3058, the Word of Blake's Toyama faction began providing Chancellor Sun-Tzu Liao with technicians and material resources to finish overhauling the facility, reportedly as repayment of a personal debt. This assistance accelerated the development of several new designs, with the Jinggau walking off the assembly line in early 3059. Production was halted for over a year after the initial run revealed that both arm sections required extensive redesign, but by 3060 the line had resumed in limited numbers.

The Jinggau quickly proved its worth during the Capellan-St. Ives War, where its combination of speed, firepower, and armor made it an ideal spearhead for Capellan offensive operations. As production increased, the design saw service with elite units including the Tau Ceti Rangers, Warrior Houses, and the Death Commandos. The Shengli Arms facility continued to develop variants through the Civil War period, introducing the plasma rifle-armed JN-G7L and the stealth-capable JN-G9CC during the Jihad. However, the Word of Blake Jihad inflicted devastating damage on Shengli Arms when renegade elements attacked in late 3068, crippling production lines and causing an estimated eighty-four percent loss of capital and personnel. The facility eventually restored Jinggau production to limited capacity, operating at roughly sixty-three percent output by 3079.

The design's fortunes shifted dramatically during the Victoria War when the Federated Suns invaded Victoria in 3103. The Fifth Capellan Defense Force, unwilling to let Shengli Arms fall to the enemy, razed the facility entirely. The Federated Suns subsequently sold the gutted plant to Kallon Industries, which refurbished it to produce Davion designs instead. For over four decades, no new Jinggaus left the Victoria production lines, though significant numbers remained in service across multiple nations through salvage, battlefield capture, and the Clan Hell's Horses refit programs that emerged after Operation SCOUR in 3078.

The Jinggau's renaissance came in 3145 when the CCAF recaptured Victoria. Shengli's engineers initially presented a modernized design under the "Jinggau II" designation, but Capellan officials quashed the name in favor of continuity, preferring to frame the return to Jinggau production as a restoration of normalcy rather than a new beginning. The resulting JN-G9B incorporated Clan Sea Fox-supplied technology alongside domestic innovations, producing a formidable modern combatant that surprised Republic Armed Forces defenders during Operation Clarity with its triple-strength myomer-enhanced speed and increased survivability. By the ilClan era, the Jinggau had become a truly multi-national design, with original Capellan production models, Clan-technology refits, and mixed-tech conversions serving across the Inner Sphere in the forces of the Confederation, Federated Suns, Free Worlds League, Republic remnants, and Clan Hell's Horses alike.

text.deployment: This variant is a lower-technology production variant introduced in 3146 that replaces the Clan-specification Streak SRM-6 launchers with standard Inner Sphere SRM-6 systems. This trade sacrifices the ammunition efficiency and guaranteed-hit accuracy of the Streak system in exchange for greater flexibility in munitions selection and simplified maintenance logistics. The variant was developed as Irian BattleMechs Unlimited sought to increase production output without relying entirely on Clan component supply chains, ensuring the Free Worlds League Military could field more Julianos even if access to Clan-manufactured launchers proved inconsistent.
text.battleHistory:
The Juliano's history is inextricably linked to the political fortunes of the Free Worlds League's successor states. Development began in the early thirty-second century within the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth, one of several states that emerged following the dissolution of the Free Worlds League during the Jihad. The Commonwealth's leadership sought to establish military self-sufficiency by producing a native assault BattleMech, and Irian BattleMechs Unlimited's facility on Angell II was tasked with the project.

Production commenced around 3116, and the Juliano quickly earned its place as the signature 'Mech of the realm. The Commonwealth jealously guarded its new creation, forbidding all export of the design. For roughly twenty years, the Juliano served as a symbol of Marik-Stewart military power and was deployed exclusively within Commonwealth forces.

The reformation of the Free Worlds League in the early 3140s brought the Juliano into broader service. The new FWLM inherited the design and maintained the export ban while assigning new-build Julianos to front-line formations, particularly the Tamarind Regulars tasked with operations along the Lyran border. The Eighth Tamarind Regulars especially received large numbers of the design, pairing them with Awesomes in assault lance formations.

The Fourth Battle of Tamarind in 3142 provided the Juliano's first major combat debut under League colors. During fighting along the Zanzibar River at Point Bravo, a mixed assault lance of the Eighth Regulars equipped with Julianos engaged a Lyran Guards assault lance whose 'Mechs had already expended much of their ammunition in sustained combat. The engagement demonstrated the Juliano's defining tactical advantage: its ability to sustain combat long after ammunition-dependent opponents had spent their stores, tearing apart the Lyran formation in a devastating combination of laser and missile fire.

Beyond the League, Clan Wolf acquired a limited number of Julianos as salvage during its invasion of Marik-Stewart territory, assigning these captured machines to second-line Clusters. The introduction of the JLN-5B and JLN-5C variants in 3146 expanded the Juliano family, with Irian BattleMechs Unlimited demonstrating both the ability to simplify the design for increased production and to push it to its technological limits with full Clan-specification armament.

text.deployment: Introduced alongside the JLN-5B in 3146, this variant takes the opposite approach by upgrading the entire weapons suite to Clan specifications. The three Extended-Range Large Lasers are replaced with their superior Clan-grade equivalents, while the Extended-Range Medium Lasers give way to Clan Medium Pulse Lasers for improved accuracy at close range. The Clan Streak SRM-6 launchers are retained from the base model. The result is the most devastating variant in the Juliano family, a reflection of Irian BattleMechs Unlimited's growing capability to produce full Clan-technology weapon systems for the reformed Free Worlds League.

text.deployment: A custom configuration assembled from necessity rather than design, this variant was created after a heavily damaged Karhu was salvaged following the death of its original pilot in 3085. While the Clan-technology base chassis was maintained, the replacement OmniPods use exclusively Inner Sphere components. A retractable blade and Inner Sphere plasma rifle occupy the right arm, while a heavy PPC and standard-grade ER medium laser fill the left arm. Two tons of plasma rifle ammunition provide adequate endurance. The configuration also mounts a Beagle active probe, Guardian ECM suite, and C3 slave unit, integrating it into Inner Sphere command networks and giving it respectable electronic warfare capability despite its mixed-technology nature. The use of IS-grade components results in a significantly lower combat effectiveness compared to standard configurations, but the C3 integration makes this variant valuable as part of a coordinated lance.

Configured for longer-range engagement profiles, the A configuration mounts a Gauss rifle in the right arm supported by a left-torso LRM-10, giving the Karhu credible standoff firepower. The addition of a large pulse laser, ER medium laser, and micro pulse laser in the right arm ensures the configuration remains dangerous at close range should an enemy close the distance. Two tons of Gauss ammunition and one ton of missile reloads provide reasonable endurance for sustained operations, while five standard jump jets maintain the mobility expected of the chassis. The A configuration sees frequent deployment in mixed formations where its combination of precision long-range fire and jump capability allows it to anchor defensive positions while retaining the ability to reposition quickly.

A dedicated short-range brawler, the B configuration leverages the Karhu's mobility to devastating effect by mounting a massive Ultra AC/20 in the left arm. Three ER medium lasers in the right arm supplement the autocannon's fearsome close-range damage output, while a targeting computer enhances accuracy across all weapons. Four tons of autocannon ammunition provide adequate endurance for intense engagements, and jump jets allow the configuration to navigate urban terrain and exploit cover. The addition of an ECM suite provides electronic warfare capability, making the B configuration a particularly deadly city fighter. Two additional double heat sinks help manage the thermal load generated by sustained fire from the autocannon and laser battery.

The C configuration offers a balanced mixed-range loadout, mounting dual Ultra AC/5 autocannons split between the side torsos for sustained suppressive fire at medium to long range. An ER large laser and ER medium laser in the left arm provide energy-based firepower that complements the autocannons without ammunition dependency, while a retractable blade in the right arm maintains the Karhu's characteristic close-combat capability. Each autocannon carries a ton of ammunition, and jump jets preserve the design's trademark mobility. The C configuration's versatile weapon mix makes it well-suited for extended patrol and garrison duties where ammunition resupply may be limited.

The D configuration represents the Karhu's most electronics-intensive loadout, built around a pair of ER PPCs in the left arm supported by three ER medium lasers in the right arm and a Streak SRM-6 in the left torso. A comprehensive electronics suite including a targeting computer, active probe, and ECM suite transforms the configuration into a potent command and reconnaissance platform. Dual anti-missile systems provide active defenses against incoming missiles, while four additional double heat sinks manage the substantial thermal output of the twin PPCs. With the highest operational cost among standard configurations, the D stands as a significant investment but delivers exceptional capability for independent operations and deep raids where its combination of firepower, electronic warfare, and active defenses allows it to operate effectively without support.

Developed in 3099, the G configuration introduces a supercharger that pushes the Karhu's top speed to one hundred kilometers per hour, making it one of the fastest heavy OmniMechs in the Dominion's arsenal. A one-hundred-fifty-meter jump capability further enhances its ability to evade return fire and control engagement ranges. The primary weapon is an improved heavy large laser, supported by three ER medium lasers and four Streak SRM-4 launchers that provide devastating close-range salvos. A light TAG system allows the G configuration to designate targets for artillery and semi-guided munitions, expanding its role beyond direct combat into fire support coordination. The G configuration reflects a post-Jihad design philosophy emphasizing speed and flexibility over raw firepower.

First deployed in 3079, this variant configuration arrived too late to participate in Operation SCOUR but quickly established itself as a cavalry 'Mech in the Dominion's post-Jihad touman. The combination of a retractable blade and plasma cannon appeals to warriors who favor close-quarters combat, while the ER PPC provides effective fire at longer ranges. Improved jump jets grant this variant configuration outstanding maneuverability for a heavy OmniMech, allowing it to exploit terrain and close rapidly with opponents. The design's skull-like chassis sculpting and oversized right-hand claw serve both as functional weapons and as deliberate psychological warfare tools intended to inspire fear, a quality that resonates with the Dominion's increasingly assertive military posture.

text.notes: Features the following Design Quirk: Bad Reputation, Easy to Maintain.

text.overview:
The King Crab was designed in 2741 by Cosara Weaponries at the direct request of General Aleksandr Kerensky for an assault 'Mech capable of crippling or destroying another BattleMech in a single salvo. Filling the role of a devastating close-range combatant, the hundred-ton King Crab earned its fearsome reputation through the raw destructive power of its twin super-heavy autocannons, mounted in distinctive claw-like arm housings that gave the design its name. Though initially envisioned as a potential command vehicle, the King Crab proved less suited to that capacity than expected, a role ultimately filled by the Atlas.

Production was centered at Cosara facilities on Mars and Northwind under Star League authority, with the design seeing widespread service in the SLDF. The devastation of the Succession Wars reduced the King Crab to near-extinction, but ComStar's secret preservation of the Mars factory ensured the design's survival and eventual return to mass production in the thirty-first century.
text.capabilities:
The King Crab's tactical doctrine is straightforward: close with the enemy and deliver overwhelming firepower. Its primary armament of twin Deathgiver Autocannon/20s represents one of the most destructive weapon pairings ever mounted on a BattleMech, capable of stripping the armor from virtually any opponent in a few devastating salvos. The autocannons are housed within reinforced arm assemblies fitted with simple hand actuators that function as protective cowlings, giving the 'Mech its distinctive crab-like silhouette and the appearance of pincers opening and closing in combat. A Simpson-15 LRM launcher and Exostar large laser provide secondary fire support at longer ranges, ensuring the King Crab is not entirely helpless during its approach to engagement range.

Sixteen tons of Aldis X ferro-fibrous armor provide solid, evenly distributed protection across the chassis, with CASE safeguarding the ammunition stores from catastrophic detonation. The arms represent a notable vulnerability, however, as an internal hit to either limb can knock an autocannon out of the fight entirely. The King Crab's most significant limitation is its dependence on ammunition; each autocannon draws from a mere five-round magazine, giving pilots limited sustained firepower before running dry. Combined with a modest top speed of 54 kilometers per hour and a well-earned reputation as a maintenance-intensive design, the King Crab demands careful tactical employment and reliable logistics to realize its devastating potential.
text.deployment: Introduced in 3143 as a factory-produced version of a successful field modification, this variant replaces the standard KGC-009's autocannons and missile launchers with Clan-specification Hyper-Assault Gauss Rifles, dramatically increasing ranged firepower. The medium lasers give way to Clan-grade ER small lasers, while Clan plasma rifles replace the Inner Sphere models for improved performance. Produced by StarCorps Industries at Loburg, this hybrid design demonstrates the increasing availability of Clan technology to Inner Sphere manufacturers during the Dark Age period, offering Lyran forces a significant upgrade in striking power while retaining the KGC-009's robust chassis and heavy armor protection.
text.battleHistory:
The King Crab's origins trace to 2741, when General Aleksandr Kerensky personally commissioned Cosara Weaponries to design an assault 'Mech of unmatched destructive power. The resulting design exceeded expectations, and production commenced at Cosara's facilities on Mars and Northwind. The King Crab served with distinction in the SLDF throughout the final decades of the Star League, though it never displaced the Atlas as the preferred command vehicle for senior officers. When the Amaris Civil War erupted in 2767, Republican forces destroyed the Mars factory, leaving only the Northwind facility operational.

The Exodus of 2784 dealt the King Crab a severe blow, as General Kerensky's departing forces took the vast majority of existing King Crabs with them, including the entire production run of the prototype KGC-010. The Northwind factory's destruction in 2786, an early casualty of the First Succession War, effectively ended new production in the Inner Sphere. The King Crab's relatively simple construction meant surviving examples were easier to maintain than many Star League-era designs, but attrition took its toll. By the close of the Third Succession War, only a handful remained in active service with the Great Houses, each one a prized and jealously guarded asset.

ComStar's seizure of Terra through Operation Silver Shield proved critical to the King Crab's survival. The order's technicians repaired and mothballed the damaged Mars factory, secretly stockpiling King Crabs for future use. By the early thirty-first century, ComStar contracted Cosara Weaponries to quietly resume production to replenish their aging reserves, equipping the Com Guards with refurbished and newly built King Crabs. The looming threat of the Clan Invasion spurred the development of the KGC-001 "Clanbuster" variant in 3052, which proved so successful at the Battle of Tukayyid that ComStar authorized general market sales from both the Mars and Northwind plants, with Cosara receiving a share of profits.

The Word of Blake's conquest of Terra and subsequent seizure of the Northwind factory in 3069 upended King Crab production once again. The Blakists retooled the Northwind line to produce their own variants, including the jump-capable KGC-008 for Protectorate forces. ComStar responded with an uncharacteristically bold move, dispatching a mercenary espionage team to infiltrate the Northwind facility and steal the new design specifications. These plans were then offered to StarCorps Industries, who eagerly began producing the KGC-007 at their Son Hoa plant for ComStar, the Lyran Alliance, and the Federated Suns alike.

The post-Jihad era saw continued evolution of the King Crab. StarCorps relocated their production line from Son Hoa to Loburg in the late 3090s, introducing the modernized KGC-009 in 3104 to meet the demands of the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces. The design proved popular with senior Lyran officers despite its continued ammunition dependency. Cosara Weaponries eventually returned the Mars facility to active production under Republic of the Sphere oversight, developing the KGC-011 with its revolutionary XXL engine for dramatically improved battlefield mobility. By the ilClan era, the King Crab remained a respected and feared assault platform, its production split between Cosara's historic Mars facility and StarCorps' Loburg plant, ensuring the design's continued presence on battlefields across the Inner Sphere.

text.overview: The Golden Unity's redesign of the King Crab has been likened to a "big brother for the Marauder" due to its weapon layout. Arm-mounted PPCs paired with light blazers replace the assault autocannons, while a single superheavy autocannon sits in a pronounced dorsal mount. Jump jets provide extra maneuverability in cluttered environments, making this variant a nasty surprise for unsuspecting enemies.
text.capabilities: The jump jets give this assault machine unexpected repositioning ability in broken terrain, allowing it to occupy firing positions that conventional assaults cannot reach. The PPCs and dorsal autocannon create overlapping engagement zones that punish enemies at every range. Pilots should use jump mobility to maintain optimal firing distance rather than wading into brawls, letting the light blazers handle anything that slips inside PPC range.
